newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Burundi refugees flocking to Tanzania, U.N. says.
newsitem.headline: Burundi refugees flocking to Tanzania, U.N. says.

text.p: Between 150 and 200 people fleeing fighting in Burundi are crossing daily into Tanzania, the United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Tuesday.
The latest arrivals, apparently overwhelmingly Hutus, have brought the total of Burundian refugees in Tanzania to over 300,000, UNHCR spokeswoman Pam O'Toole told a news briefing.
The new refugees are arriving at villages on the edge of Lake Tanganyika in Tanzania's Kigoma region and come from Burundi's Bururi and Makamba provinces, she said.
"They say there is unrest and fighting in their home villages and they fear being caught in the crossfire," she added. A total of 8,800 had arrived in Tanzania during the month of June alone.
Many Hutus have left Burundi, like its neighbour Rwanda the scene of strife between the two major ethnic groups, since the Tutsi-dominated Burundi army ousted a Hutu president last year.
O'Toole said UNHCR officials on the spot were transporting many of the new arrivals by boat around the lake to camps in the Kigoma region.
